title: HF Drive IPC 1.0
description: Normative wire contract for HF Drive provider IPC. Frame: 4-byte little-endian length (1..=1048576) followed by this envelope as UTF-8 JSON. Canonical bytes: members in UTF-8 byte-lexicographic key order (typed serializers emit declaration order, which matches for ASCII keys), compact separators, minimal string escapes (\" \\ \b \t \n \f \r and \u00xx lowercase for other C0/DEL controls), u64 fields as canonical decimal strings (no leading zeros, no sign), u32 fields as JSON integers, UUIDs lowercase hyphenated, optional fields omitted (a JSON null for an optional field decodes as absent and is never emitted), duplicate member names, unknown members, unknown enum variants, floats, and NaN/Infinity are rejected. Protocol version is exactly 1.0; only a hello request with another version is parsed (so the provider can answer with supported versions and close). List pages return items + next_cursor and accept cursor + limit (<= 200). Every mutation request carries a unique operation_id (operation UUID); reusing it must not duplicate the durable mutation. set_publication_credentials carries a user-scoped DPAPI ciphertext envelope; raw key/secret bytes never appear on the wire and this envelope is never logged.

result.description: typed result body matching the response method (#/$defs/<method>_result)

response_body.description: exactly one of result or error

method.description: snake_case method or event name; must agree with kind and body

body.description: typed body selected by kind+method (see body map below); never raw dispatch JSON

body_map.description: kind=request  -> body matches #/$defs/<method>_request; kind=response -> body matches #/$defs/response_body whose result matches #/$defs/<method>_result; kind=event    -> body matches #/$defs/<method>_event (method is one of status_changed, activity_changed, conflicts_changed).
